fields.description:
## Context / Problem
`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` (policy `d37e-4f64-3265-4f30`, wired at `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:172`) passes CLEAN on the current tree, yet the reconciler still mutates the tickets tracker outside the atomic locked transaction. It misses those writes by construction: the checker's rules R1 (raw `subprocess` git) and R2 (calls to the wrapper names `run_git`/`run_git_write`/`_run_git`/`_git`) enforce the MECHANISM rule "no raw subprocess git", and the reconciler write seam is sanctioned at MODULE granularity — every mutation primitive in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py` carries a function-level `# raw-git-ok: reconciler write seam (git_adapter/_ref_lock)` marker (see `git_adapter.py:184`, `:230`, `:246`, `:252`). Because those primitives are sanctioned exports, ANY caller may compose them into a hand-rolled non-atomic sequence and the checker approves every call individually. The PROTOCOL rule — "tracker mutations go through the atomic transaction" — is unenforced.

Proven live instance: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py:226` (`git_adapter.add`) plus `:246` (`git_adapter.commit`) stage-and-commit against the tickets tracker with no lock and no atomic commit+push.

## Approach
Add rule **R3 (seam composition)** to the EXISTING checker rather than a new script, so one gate, one marker vocabulary, and one CI wiring keep covering raw git writes. R3 closes the granularity gap precisely: it re-scopes the sanction from "every export of the wrapper module" to "the transaction seams themselves".

R3 fires on a call to a git-adapter **mutation primitive** made from outside the reconciler write-seam modules. The primitive set is `add`, `commit`, `commit_tree`, `read_tree`, `rm_cached`, `update_ref`, `write_tree` — read/query exports (`rev_parse`, `cat_file_exists`, `diff_cached_names`, `log_format`, `remote_get_url`, `verify_commit`) are excluded. `commit_email` is also excluded: despite its name it is `git log -1 --format=%ae` (`git_adapter.py:293`), a read.

Because `add`/`commit` are ubiquitous method names, R3 binds on the RECEIVER, not the bare attribute: a call fires only when the receiver is a resolved git-adapter module reference. Two binding forms, both already used in-tree, are resolved per file:
- an import binding — `from rebar_reconciler import git_adapter` (`__main__.py:321`, `apply_outbound.py:67`, `_concurrency.py:55`), including `as`-aliases;
- a dynamic-loader binding — `git_adapter = _load("rebar_reconciler.git_adapter", "git_adapter.py")` (`reconcile_helpers.py:203`), recognised by the module-path string argument.
A bare-name call also fires when the name was `from`-imported out of a git-adapter module (`from ...git_adapter import add`). Anything else is not a git-adapter call and does not fire — so `set.add(...)`, `session.commit(...)`, and friends stay silent.

Sanctioned entry set (R3 never fires inside these): the reconciler write-seam files themselves — `git_adapter.py`, `_ref_lock.py`, `_ref_lock_push.py`. Those ARE the atomic transaction; the primitives are defined and composed there under the ref lock.

Sanction elsewhere reuses the existing inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` marker with its existing semantics — line-level or enclosing-function, reason mandatory, no external allowlist file. Reusing the marker (rather than minting a second one) keeps a single sanction vocabulary and means the `marker-without-reason` violation already covers R3.

**Riskiest assumption, checked first:** that R3's receiver binding produces no false positives across `src/` and `scripts/` — the rule would be unusable if ordinary `.add(`/`.commit(` calls fired. The cheapest falsifying check is running `--report` over the tree and confirming every new hit is a real git-adapter call; that runs before any marker is written.

## Scope
- `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` — add R3: the primitive set, the per-file git-adapter binding resolver, the seam-internal file set, and the emission; extend the module docstring's policy statement. Keep R1/R2, the marker semantics, and the fail-closed classes unchanged.
- `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` — R3 unit tests against synthetic trees, matching the existing fixture style.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py` — a durable reasoned marker on `_commit_binding_store_snapshot`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py` — a durable reasoned marker on `_purge_committed_reconciler_locks`.

## Site dispositions (enumerated from the rule's first run; recorded in full as a ticket comment)
Both remaining out-of-transaction sites take a **durable reasoned marker** — neither is a "drains later" debt baseline.

1. `reconcile_helpers.py:226/246` — `_commit_binding_store_snapshot`. Ticket `6454-d06e-7361-4e3d` was scoped to convert this and deliberately did NOT: its closed description records that routing through `rebar._store.push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch` (which stages `git add -A`) sweeps in `.bridge_state/last-pass.json`, which the selective 5-file staging excludes, advancing the tickets HEAD on every idempotent pass and turning `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py::test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head` RED. The marker cites that boundary; follow-up ticket `11a9-b11b-e93d-4832` owns giving the seam a pathspec so the marker can be deleted.
2. `__main__.py:338-351` — `_purge_committed_reconciler_locks`. Composes `read_tree`/`rm_cached`/`write_tree`/`commit_tree`/`update_ref` in a DETACHED temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE` set at `__main__.py:337`) and CAS-advances the ref (`update_ref(..., new_commit, old)`), so it never touches the worktree or the main index and a concurrent writer is safe. A per-site marker rather than a blanket "detached-index operations are exempt" rule: detachedness comes from an `env` dict built at the call site, so it is not statically decidable from the callable, and a blanket rule would be forgeable by any future caller passing `env=`.

## Testing
Unit tests in `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py`, driven against synthetic source trees exactly as the existing tests are:
- **Happy path (fires):** a module doing `from pkg import git_adapter` then `git_adapter.add(d, "f")` and `git_adapter.commit(d, "m")` produces two `seam-composition` violations naming the primitives.
- **Sanctioned entry (does not fire):** the same composed calls inside `git_adapter.py` / `_ref_lock.py` / `_ref_lock_push.py` produce zero R3 violations.
- **Marker semantics:** the same composed calls with `# raw-git-ok: reason` on the line, and with the marker on the enclosing function, both pass; a bare `# raw-git-ok:` with no reason still fails as `marker-without-reason`.
- **False-positive floor (edge):** `s = set(); s.add(x)` and `session.commit()` in a module with no git-adapter binding produce zero violations; a read-only `git_adapter.rev_parse(...)` / `git_adapter.commit_email(...)` produces zero violations.
- **Dynamic-loader binding:** `git_adapter = _load("rebar_reconciler.git_adapter", "git_adapter.py")` followed by `git_adapter.commit(...)` fires.
- **Whole-tree regression:** `check(REPO_ROOT)` returns no violations with the markers in place (the existing tree-clean test covers R1/R2; R3 joins it).

## Non-goals
Remediating the two sanctioned sites (ticket `11a9-b11b-e93d-4832` owns the binding-snapshot one; the legacy-lock purge is a migration slated for deletion), changing `git_adapter`'s API, and runtime interception.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] R3 exists in `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` and fires on a git-adapter mutation-primitive call outside the seam; verified by the new unit tests passing (`pytest tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py`).
- [ ] R3 does NOT fire inside `git_adapter.py`, `_ref_lock.py`, or `_ref_lock_push.py`; verified by the sanctioned-entry unit test.
- [ ] R3 does NOT fire on non-git-adapter `.add(`/`.commit(` calls or on read-only git-adapter exports; verified by the false-positive-floor unit test.
- [ ] Marker semantics hold for R3: a reasoned `# raw-git-ok:` (line or enclosing function) sanctions the hit; a reasonless marker still fails; verified by the marker unit tests.
- [ ] Both enumerated sites carry a durable reasoned inline marker stating the concrete justification (not a "TBD"/"will be removed" placeholder); verified by reading the two diffs and by `python scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` exiting 0 on the tree.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py --report` lists every R3 hit with its reason; the `check` run reports zero unsanctioned violations (exit 0).
- [ ] `make lint` (incl. the complexity ratchet) and `make typecheck` exit 0.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The change lands via Gerrit at `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`; the operator records the change number and both vote outcomes as a ticket comment.
